answer: Graph-based trust propagation mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding random-walk flows from trusted seed nodes across peer networks. Autonomous nodes cataloging yarrow across a community garden or wetland delta exchange signed interaction proofs. An attacker incurs the verifiable topological cost of securing scarce trust edges from honest peers per identity. However, compromising even one well-connected node allows an adversary to bleed substantial trust into fraudulent subgraphs.
